A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SemiCP with Nearest Neighbor Matching. All 24 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including experimental and theoretical appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix H report original benchmark results, ablations, conditional-coverage experiments, and distribution-shift evaluations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I retain original empirical evaluations and add SAPS results; Appendix G also reports calibration runtimes.

M1.justification: The NNM bias correction, pooled-score quantile, conditional extension, randomized-score adaptation, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Revised proof assumptions and newly documented binary-search implementation do not establish a changed prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, conditional classification, and shifts involving ImageNet-R, ImageNet-S, and ImageNet-V2. SAPS and runtime experiments use retained datasets and tasks. Class-conditional results remain in the text despite removal of their separate plot.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix I.2 and Figure 10 newly evaluate SAPS-based Standard and Oracle comparisons against SemiCP; v1 only cited SAPS. Existing THR/APS/RAPS, Interpolation, ClusterCP, and bias-estimation and neighborhood-selection comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds randomized SAPS with weight 0.01 and calibration-only timing that excludes inference and test-time prediction. The motivating calibration-size experiment changes from averaging three scores to APS alone, with fewer displayed calibration sizes. Main benchmark splits, backbones, metrics, and RAPS settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's pseudo-bias distribution comparison is replaced by a direct comparison of naive, NNM, and true score distributions in v2 Figure 3. V2 also adds computational-overhead analysis. Existing bias-estimator, neighborhood, pseudo-label-accuracy, and distribution-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the 1,000-trial benchmark convention, 100-trial distribution-shift evaluation, and standard-error reporting in Table 2. Added experiments use existing repetition conventions; no new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds SAPS curves and runtime results, including 0.001583 seconds for SemiCP versus 0.000216 for Standard. It revises the CIFAR-10 headline reductions from 76%/7% to 77%/5.7%, and makes the Standard reference constant in the unlabeled-size sweep. Tables 2–4 are numerically unchanged; the separate class-conditional curves disappear while example values remain.

T1.justification: V1's two propositions are substantially replaced by three theorems addressing distribution-mismatch bias, calibration-conditional concentration, and a uniform NNM CDF approximation bound. The consistency proof replaces feature-neighborhood restrictions with density, Lipschitz, and Markov assumptions. V2 also adds a proof of the existing Beta-distribution result and computational-complexity analysis.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds a new quantitative claim that coverage-gap error decreases at O(1/sqrt(N)) toward a residual error term. This substantially expands v1's central theoretical contribution of asymptotic score-distribution consistency and coverage validity, while retaining the SemiCP framework and empirical applicability claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses the tradeoff between stability and coverage bias. It reinterprets the retained pseudo-label-accuracy experiment as a failure case at low accuracy, whereas v1 emphasized robustness with moderate accuracy. The limitations also newly state that regression has not been addressed.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents sorting and binary search for NNM, TorchCP usage, an RTX 4090 GPU, and the scope of calibration timing. It also supplies the SAPS weight and randomization choice. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained benchmark implementations.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against Mazuelas's unsupervised calibration method and discusses CPSSDS and CSForest, distinguishing their optimization or application roles from SemiCP. Several peripheral references disappear. Publication and bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before preliminaries, the small-calibration theoretical discussion moves into the main text, duplicated motivation is removed, and the appendices are reorganized. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, adds a method-overview figure, replaces the motivating and distribution-diagnostic graphics, adds SAPS plots and a runtime table, and removes the separate class-conditional panel. Existing plots and tables are resized and rearranged, and the notation table becomes prose.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, adds useful SAPS/runtime evidence, and states failure conditions more clearly. However, its new headline convergence-rate claim relies on Appendix B.1–B.2 applying an i.i.d. mixture argument without establishing that it describes the pooled NNM scores, which share the labeled calibration set in Algorithm 1. This unresolved justification for a substantially stronger central claim prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
